name: Food trivia (easy)
description: 50 easy questions about dishes, ingredients, cuisines, cooking terms. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: Which Italian city is the birthplace of the Margherita pizza?
items.explain: Pizza Margherita comes from Naples, the city where modern pizza developed.

items.question: Pizza Margherita is traditionally said to be named after which royal?
items.explain: The pizza was named for Queen Margherita of Savoy, who visited Naples in 1889.

source.title: The History & Evolution of Pizza Margherita

items.question: Which fruit is the main ingredient of guacamole?
items.explain: Guacamole is a dip or spread made of peeled, mashed ripe avocados plus other ingredients.

items.question: Why is lime juice often added to guacamole?
answers: To turn the dip bright green
items.explain: Lime juice slows oxidation, which is what makes cut avocado turn brown.

items.question: Guacamole was already part of the cuisine of which civilization when the Spanish arrived in the 16th century?
items.explain: By the time of the Spanish conquest, guacamole was an established part of Aztec cuisine.

items.question: Which legume is the main ingredient of hummus?
items.explain: Hummus is made from cooked, mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice and garlic.

items.question: Tahini, a key ingredient in hummus, is a paste made from which seeds?
items.explain: Tahini is a sesame paste, which is why sesame is a declared allergen in hummus.

items.question: Tofu is made by curdling milk made from which bean?
items.explain: Tofu is made by coagulating soy milk, which is extracted from ground soybeans.

source.title: How to Make Tofu - Chopstick Chronicles

items.question: Tofu is also commonly known by which other name?
items.explain: Tofu is also called bean curd because it is made from coagulated soy milk.

source.title: Easy Recipe: Make Tofu from Soy Milk at Home

items.question: In which Spanish region does the rice dish paella originate?
items.explain: Paella comes from the Valencia region, where it began as a lunch for farm workers.

items.question: Which expensive spice gives paella its yellow color?
items.explain: Paella is characterized by saffron, which gives the rice its yellow color and distinctive flavor.

source.title: Paella, the traditional Spanish dish from Valencia

items.question: The dish paella takes its name from the word for which piece of cookware?
items.explain: The dish is named after the wide, shallow pan traditionally used to cook it over an open fire.

items.question: Kimchi is a staple dish of the cuisine of which country?
items.explain: Kimchi is a traditional Korean dish of fermented vegetables, most often cabbage.

source.title: What is Kimchi & How Do You Make?

items.question: Which preparation process turns cabbage into kimchi?
items.explain: Kimchi is made by fermenting salted and seasoned cabbage, which gives it its sour tang.

source.title: What is Kimchi & How Do You Make?

items.question: Which Italian city is the original home of pesto?
items.explain: Pesto originated in the Ligurian city of Genoa and is used to dress pasta.

items.question: Which herb is the main ingredient in classic Genovese pesto?
items.explain: Classic pesto genovese is built on basil, blended with olive oil, cheese, pine nuts and garlic.

items.question: Which nut is traditionally used in authentic Genovese pesto?
items.explain: Pine nuts are the traditional nut in pesto genovese. Other nuts are mainly used outside Italy.

items.question: What seasoning gives sushi rice its characteristic tang and sets it apart from plain steamed rice?
items.explain: Sushi is defined by its vinegared rice, which is typically seasoned with sugar and salt as well.

items.question: What is the Japanese dish of thinly sliced raw fish served without sushi rice called?
items.explain: Sashimi is thinly sliced raw fish or meat served without rice. Sushi, by contrast, is any dish made with vinegared rice.

items.question: Which style of sushi, the most commonly recognized today, places seafood on a hand-pressed bed of vinegared rice?
items.explain: Nigiri-zushi is the familiar style in which a slice of seafood sits on a small hand-pressed mound of vinegared rice.

items.question: In the earliest forms of sushi, fermenting rice was a way to stop which food from spoiling?
items.explain: Sushi began as a preservation method, in which lacto-fermentation of the rice prevented the fish from spoiling.

items.question: Which short-grain rice, named after a town in Italy's Po Valley, is traditionally used to make risotto?
items.explain: Arborio rice is named after the town of Arborio in the Po Valley and is the best-known rice for risotto.

source.title: taking the risk out of risotto

items.question: What do the rice grains release while being stirred slowly in hot stock, giving risotto its creamy texture?
items.explain: Risotto is cooked slowly with stock and stirred until the rice releases its starch, which makes the dish creamy.

source.title: Easy Garlic Parmesan Risotto Recipe (VIDEO) - Kylee Cooks

items.question: The Italian cooking term "al dente", used for pasta, literally means what?
items.explain: "Al dente" means "to the tooth" in Italian. It describes pasta that is cooked but still has a little firmness when you bite it.

items.question: The spice saffron is made from the dried stigmas of which flower?
items.explain: Saffron comes from the stigmas of the autumn-flowering saffron crocus, Crocus sativus.

items.question: Why is saffron such an expensive spice?
answers: Only a tiny part of each flower is used, and it is picked by hand
The plants can only be grown on one small island
The threads must be aged in barrels for many years
The flowers bloom only once every ten years
items.correct: Only a tiny part of each flower is used, and it is picked by hand
items.explain: Each flower has only three stigmas, and harvesting must be done by hand. It takes about 75,000 flowers to make a pound of saffron.

items.question: Saffron is an important ingredient in which classic French fish soup?
items.explain: Britannica names saffron as an important ingredient in bouillabaisse, the fish soup from the south of France.

items.question: Chocolate is made from the processed seeds of which tree?
items.explain: Cocoa beans are the processed seeds of the cacao tree, Theobroma cacao, and chocolate is made from them.

items.question: Cacao trees, the source of chocolate, originally come from which part of the world?
items.explain: Chocolate comes from the cacao tree, which is originally from Central and South America.

items.question: White chocolate is made from sugar, milk and which part of the cacao bean?
items.explain: White chocolate contains cocoa butter, sugar and milk but no cocoa solids, which is why it is pale.

source.title: How Cocoa Beans Become Chocolate: A Step-by-Step Guide

items.question: Vanilla, a popular flavoring, is obtained from the seed pods of which type of plant?
items.explain: Vanilla is a spice derived from orchids of the genus Vanilla, mainly from the pods of the flat-leaved vanilla orchid.

items.question: In which country is the vanilla orchid native, even though most vanilla is now grown elsewhere?
items.explain: Vanilla planifolia is native to Mexico. Madagascar is now a major producer, but the plant did not originate there.

source.title: Medicinal Spices Exhibit - UCLA Biomedical Library: History & Special Collections

items.question: How are the seafood and vegetables cooked in the Japanese dish tempura?
answers: Dipped in a thin batter and deep-fried
Simmered slowly in a soy broth
items.correct: Dipped in a thin batter and deep-fried
items.explain: Tempura is seafood and vegetables coated in a thin batter and deep-fried.

items.question: Which European country is credited with bringing the batter-frying technique that became tempura to Japan?
items.explain: The forerunner of tempura first appeared in Nagasaki in the late 16th century, brought over by Portuguese traders and missionaries.

items.question: Overmixing tempura batter activates which wheat protein, making the fried coating soft and dough-like instead of crisp?
items.explain: Tempura batter is mixed only briefly, leaving lumps, because overmixing activates wheat gluten and ruins the crisp texture.

items.question: In Egypt, falafel is most often made from ground versions of which bean?
items.explain: In Egypt and the Arabian Peninsula falafel is most often made with fava beans. In the Levant it is usually made with chickpeas.

items.question: Gazpacho, the cold vegetable soup, comes from which region of southern Spain?
items.explain: Gazpacho originates in Andalusia in southern Spain and is mostly eaten in summer because it is cold and refreshing.

items.question: Which ingredient, added in the 19th century, gave gazpacho its familiar red color?
items.explain: Red gazpacho was created in the 19th century when tomatoes were added to the ingredients.

items.question: Which soft Italian cheese is used to make the creamy layer of tiramisu?
items.explain: Tiramisu is covered with a cream of egg yolks, sugar and mascarpone.

items.question: In the Italian dessert tiramisu, the ladyfingers are soaked in which drink?
items.explain: Tiramisu is made with coffee-soaked ladyfingers (savoiardi) layered with a mascarpone cream and dusted with cocoa.

items.question: What does the German word "sauerkraut" literally mean?
items.explain: Sauerkraut is German for "sour cabbage". It is finely cut cabbage fermented by lactic acid bacteria.

items.question: Mayonnaise is a thick emulsion of oil, vinegar or lemon juice, and which other main ingredient?
items.explain: Mayonnaise is a stable emulsion of oil, egg yolks, and either vinegar or lemon juice. The egg yolk acts as the emulsifier.

items.question: Wasabi, the pungent green paste served with sushi, is also known as Japanese what?
items.explain: Wasabi is also called Japanese horseradish. It belongs to the same plant family as horseradish and mustard.

items.question: Traditional couscous is made of small steamed granules of which wheat product?
items.explain: Couscous is made from semolina grains, which are the endosperm of durum wheat, rolled and steamed.

items.question: Couscous is a traditional dish of which part of the world?
items.explain: Britannica describes couscous as a North African dish of semolina and accompanying foods.

items.question: Which fiery red pepper sauce is traditionally eaten with couscous and its stew?
items.explain: Couscous and its stew were traditionally eaten with harissa, a fiery sauce of red pepper and other spices.

items.question: Couscous is traditionally steamed in a special two-part pot. What is it called?
items.explain: A couscousière has a lower compartment for the stew or broth and an upper perforated part where the couscous steams.

items.question: A roux, used to thicken sauces and soups, is made by cooking flour with which ingredient?
items.explain: A roux is flour and fat cooked together in roughly equal parts by weight, and the fat is most often butter.

items.question: Which of these classic French sauces is thickened with a roux?
items.explain: Roux is used in three of the five French mother sauces: béchamel, velouté and espagnole.

items.question: As a roux is cooked longer and turns darker, what happens to its thickening power?
items.explain: The darker the roux, the less thickening power it has. A chocolate-colored roux thickens about one-fourth as much as a white roux.
